note: Erik 2026-10-04: "Put some authoring onto what exists under the ground. The mining of the earth's core fueled the nanite and power, but it also allowed true sunlight equivalence in some areas in the underground, and it goes deep. The missing 1/3 is partially due to harvesting the core." Authored by Aevi (PO). Extends world_framing.the_world_is_named (the world is a third the size it was) and the_substrate.naniteField (nanite is grounded in what pre-Transition people were doing in a place). Surfaced to the GM through the loreRefs of the deep places.
principle: Exesa goes down a long way, and what is under it is not only rock. Before the Transition, the craving for power to drive the old nanotechnology reached past the surface and into the world's core. People sank bores toward the core and drew it up: heat, metal, and the pressure-made matter the nanite of that age was made from and ran on. That harvest fed the nanite and the power of the age. It is part of why the world is a third the size it was. Not all of it: the rest was the small eating, everywhere, one working at a time. But the core is where the largest bites were taken, and the world is hollower at its heart than a world should be.

theHarvest.what: The core-harvest. Bores, shafts wide enough to lose a town in, sunk from the surface and from the deep places toward the core, with engines along them that drew the core upward and turned it into power and into nanite stock. The nanite of the old age was made from the world's own heart.
theHarvest.whoDidIt: People. The same pre-Transition people who ate the surface, not the Precursors. The lattice is Precursor work; the harvest was a human answer to a human craving. Some of the bores follow the lattice's buried lines down, and nobody now living knows whether the harvesters found those ways or were shown them.
theHarvest.whenItStopped: At the Transition, when the decision was made to cast off the technology and evolve past needing it, the harvest was stopped: the bores capped, the engines along them stilled. Mostly. Nobody can say all of them, because nobody alive has walked all of them.
theHarvest.whatItLeft: The bores, capped and uncapped. Spent workings on their walls. Core-heat that still rises through them, because a hollowed core is still hot. And the kept suns.
theHarvest.whyTheNaniteFieldHasADeepHalf: Nanite sits where pre-Transition people put it to work (SNG-382). Along the bores they were making it from the core, so the ground there is thick with it: ordered where someone still keeps the cycle, as the Enginewrights do in the ways under the Gearlands, and wild where nobody does.

theKeptSuns.what: The harvest brought the core's heat up, and in some places the old works turned it into light. Not lamp-light, not phosphor, not the glow of a working: true sunlight equivalence. The full spread of a day's sun, warmth on the skin, a dawn and a dusk on a cycle somebody set and nobody now can change. Under a kept sun wheat grows, skin browns, and birds that were carried down generations ago have forgotten there is any other sky.
theKeptSuns.where: In some areas, not all. A kept sun hangs in the roof of a vault large enough to carry it, usually where a bore passed close. Most of the under-world is dark; the lit places are islands in it, and travellers find them by the warmth in the rock before they see the light.
theKeptSuns.whatTheyAreCalled: Underfolk call them kept suns. Surface folk call them undersuns. The Umbrals call them the loud places.
theKinds: Tended: fields and orchards a day's walk across under one sun, farmed by whoever holds the vault. The under-world eats from these.
High vaults: a kept sun in a roof so far up that the vault keeps its own weather, with cloud under the sun and rain on the fields.

Wild: the cycle failed and the light never sets. The growth beneath has not stopped for centuries. It is wild nanite's bloom below ground, the Greenmarch's conditions with no winter and no night to check them.
Gone out: a dead orchard in the dark, and the shape of a sun still on the ceiling.
theKeptSuns.andTheUmbrals: The Umbrals do not live under kept suns and do not want to; their dark is their light, and the Underlight is home. A kept sun near Umbral ground is a border, and often a quarrel.

itGoesDeep.principle: Depth on the map is a stratum, not a distance. The authored places reach the fifth. The bores go further, and what stands below is whatever the story finds there.
strata: One down, the Near Under: cellars, holds, delves and the long stairs, within reach of the surface. Dwarven country. The Slow Stair's upper flights, the Lampless Market, the Archive Hollow, the Regulator Chamber under the Crossing.
Two down, the Lit Deeps: the first great vaults and most of the kept suns. This is where the under-world is farmed, and where the warmth starts to come up through the floor.
Three down, the Great Works and the dark cities: the Underlight, the Great Engine, the Maw. The deepest places anyone lives as a people.
Four down, the Old Ways: Precursor tunnels and harvest-roads, the Service Ways and the Leaden Deep. Few live here. Things that are still running their errands do.
Five down, where the dark becomes doctrine: the Unlit Deep and the passage below it. Cults, not peoples; a civilization can live near a pole, and only a cult can live at one.
Below that, the Bores: down toward what is left of the core. Nobody who has gone to the bottom has come back with an account the others agree on.

whatTheNameAlwaysMeant: Exesa is from exedō: to gnaw hollow, to consume from within. The name was chosen for the small eating everywhere, and it was more literal than that. The world was gnawed hollow from within, at its heart. People who know about the bores say the name was always a confession.
connectsTo: What wakes beneath (EXESA, the deep clock): the stirring is under the ground, and the bores are the deepest way down to it. Those who want it awake will want the bores open; those who hold against them will want them capped.

The Service Ways: something down there is still running its original errand, and the Enginewrights are careful not to interrupt it. Whether that errand is the harvest is the story's to find out. When play goes down there, the answer is made, and then it is true.
gmMandate: Under the ground is a world, not a cellar. Tell depth by what it is like to be there: warmth in the rock means a bore or a kept sun is near; wind in a tunnel means a vault ahead; light with a dawn is a kept sun, light that never sets is a wild one.
A kept sun is daylight. Anything that needs the sun works under it, and does not work in the dark around it.
Do not over-explain the harvest. People down there know it the way surface people know the world is smaller: an old fact, with a few bad songs about it.

The bottom of the bores is unauthored, not forbidden. It is warm, it is very far down, and something there is still hot enough to light suns a long way above it. When the story goes there, make what is there: new places, peoples and powers, generated whole and kept, the way the rest of the world grows.
_generative_20261004: Erik 2026-10-04: "The world is generative so it always needs a way to grow and change." Nothing in this file closes a door on the GM. What is unauthored below is the space the story grows into.

theDeadBelow.note: Erik 2026-10-04: "There should be Afterlings in various places underground." Afterlings are canon in the_afterlings.md: undead PEOPLE, the same mind, crafts and grudges, cold, tireless, harmed by vitality. This is where they are below.
theDeadBelow.whyBelow: The under-world suits the dead who stayed. It is cold, and they are cold. Nobody down there needs them to sleep. The dark costs them nothing. And most of the deep was dug by crews, and crews die at their work. The under-world has more Afterlings per head than anywhere but Cairnsend, and fewer of them have ever heard of the Vigil.
whereTheyAre: THE LONG SHIFT, along the harvest bores. Crews who died in the bores before the Transition and did not stop: the unattended door, four centuries deep. Some are still people. They talk, they keep a tally, and they ask for news of the surface. Some have narrowed into the driven, one errand with nothing left around it, and a crew that wanders too far down meets them. The Boreborn of the Hanging Weather are those crews' descendants. Some of the dead below are their own grandmothers many times removed, and the Capwardens go down to talk to them.

THE DROWNED OF UNDERMERE. The black lake takes boats. Some of the people in them come back up to the quays and keep working, as the dyke-crews do in the Palelands. The Lake-Queen's court counts them as subjects, not as dead.

THE SHIFT-KEEPERS OF DEEPMARK. Dwarves who die in a collapse are dug out and asked. Those who choose to stay keep the collapsed ways, which they know better than anyone living. In Deepmark, being asked is the custom, and the Vigil holds the kingdom up as proof that the asking can be done.
THE KEEPERS OF THE DEAD SUNS. Where a kept sun went out, whoever was tending it sometimes stayed. The Orchard Gone Out has one, still pruning trees that died standing.
IN THE OLD WAYS. Enginewrights who died mapping the Service Ways and kept mapping. The Wrights do not log them, which is a policy, and do not discuss it, which is another.
theDeadBelow.andTheKeptSuns: A kept sun is daylight, and daylight is vitality. Afterlings do not live under kept suns; it aches, the way a healing laid on them hurts. Under the Long Noon, where the life never stops, it is agony. So the lit deeps are the living's, and the dark strata are where the dead below keep house. The border runs where the light stops.
theDeadBelow.andThePolitics: Cairnsend's one question, consent, reaches down here too. The Grave-Callers recruit from the Long Shift, since a crew already working needs no raising. The Vigil sends envoys down to tell the deep dead that there is a town where what they are is ordinary. Most of them have never been asked anything at all.
theDeadBelow.gmMandate: Afterlings are people, not monsters. Meet them as people: a name, a door, a want, a grudge. A deep place with a crew, a collapse or a drowning in its past can have its dead who stayed, and the GM makes them when play goes there, whole, by the same rules as any person. The driven are the danger. The Afterlings are the neighbours.
